transport.boundary: ROM supports UART recovery, but the reference board needs the documented BOOT0/UART five-wire modification.

feature.boundary: Canonical LZW/raw/CRC and AGASC round trips are regression-tested.
SRAM execution and selected native/USB-loaded applications are qualified; the open HAL is incremental.
GPIO AFSEL selects software versus hardware control but does not select or prove a package route; only named part/package/board/fabric combinations inherit observed routes.

The default exact L48 profile composes canonical ID32 0x4147414d at +0, zero-extended held scratch16 at +4, counter3 at +8, and W1C1 at +c. One selectable derivative replaces the bit1 self-test hook with MCU GPIO5 DATA0/OUT_EN0 as an independently routed sustained-level set source. A second selectable derivative uses the existing synchronous fabric counter to emit one reset-rearmed autonomous count==7 event, after which the source disarms and W1C bit0 clears the latched status. Negative, OR-control, and three production runs preserve the entire public32 matrix for both derivatives. GPIO5 remains software-controlled qualification stimulus; the counter derivative proves one HCLK-synchronous autonomous fabric source. Neither profile supplies a generic user-net STATUS_SET socket, asynchronous CDC contract, interrupt controller, or event ABI. The public16 and older complete-byte profiles remain replayable. Bursts/full-window decode, arbitrary placement/width, other packages, a generic overlay/bank generator, and signed/misaligned fabric semantics remain unsupported.
Release routing fails closed around qualified IO, BRAM, carry, clock, and routing evidence; this is not complete fabric coverage.
The recorded workload is not a full RV32I compliance claim; exceptions, CSRs, and interrupts remain outside it.
